subject: Qu et al. (2023)
object: Qu et al. (2023) described an infertile male with asthenozoospermia.

subject: Qu et al. (2023)
object: Qu et al. (2023) identified variants in the ADGB gene in an infertile man with asthenozoospermia. The variants disrupted the binding of ADGB to calmodulin.

subject: Qu et al. (2023)
object: Qu et al. (2023) found that male Adgb -/- mice were infertile because of reduced sperm concentration (less than 1 x 10(6)/mL) and reduced sperm motility. Spermatogenesis was abnormal, with malformed elongating and elongated spermatids, and the cauda epididymis had about twice as many apoptotic cells. ICSI with testicular spermatids led to fertilization and development to the blastocyst stage.

subject: Qu et al. (2023)
object: Using mass spectrometry, Qu et al. (2023) identified 42 candidate proteins that interact with ADGB and are involved in sperm assembly, flagella formation, and sperm motility. They confirmed that CFAP69 and SPEF2 bind to ADGB.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: Gao et al. (2025) described 3 unrelated infertile Han Chinese men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. Under light and electron microscopy, their spermatozoa showed multiple malformations of the acrosome and flagellum.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: Gao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in a cohort of 105 Han Chinese men with idiopathic asthenoteratozoospermia. In 1 infertile man they identified a homozygous frameshift variant in the ADGB gene (c.2801_2802del, p.K934Rfs*33; NM_024694.4), confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The variant was rare in the general population and was predicted to be damaging by multiple bioinformatics tools.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: In 1 infertile Han Chinese man with asthenoteratozoospermia, Gao et al. (2025) identified a homozygous missense variant in the ADGB gene (c.C3167T, p.T1056I; NM_024694.4). The variant was rare in the general population and was predicted to be damaging.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: In 1 infertile Han Chinese man with asthenoteratozoospermia, Gao et al. (2025) identified compound heterozygous missense variants in the ADGB gene (c.C3167T, p.T1056I and c.C3197T, p.A1066V; NM_024694.4). The variants were rare in the general population and were predicted to be damaging.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: In sperm from the patients, Gao et al. (2025) found through functional assays that the structural defects were associated with dysregulation of ADGB and of multiple spermatogenesis proteins. PLC-zeta was expressed normally, but calmodulin (CaM) was deficient.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: Gao et al. (2025) reported that intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) led to successful fertilization in all 3 patients. Together with the CaM deficiency in the sperm, this suggested to the authors that ICSI rather than in vitro fertilization is the best treatment for ADGB-deficient patients.

subject: Gao et al. (2025)
object: Gao et al. (2025) noted that knockout of Adgb in male mice had previously been reported to cause male infertility, with spermatogenesis defects involving the flagella and acrosome.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) described a Chinese man with primary infertility and severe idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. His sperm concentration was 2.0 x 10(6)/mL, progressive motility was below 1%, vitality was 16%, and none of his sperm had normal morphology. He had normal reproductive hormones, a 46,XY karyotype and no Y chromosome microdeletion. Abnormal heads were seen in 76.5% of sperm and abnormal flagella in 62.5%.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) reported that Papanicolaou staining of the patient's sperm showed head defects, including microcephalic and conical heads. Tail defects were also seen: short tails, acutely angled bent tails, coiled tails and tailless sperm. On transmission electron microscopy, the patient's sperm showed acrosome defects, a disorganized helix of the mitochondrial sheath, and disorganized or missing '9+2' axonemal microtubules.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) performed whole exome sequencing in 781 Chinese men with primary infertility and identified 148 ADGB variants. Under ACMG criteria, 45 were classified as benign, 1 as likely benign, 96 as of uncertain significance and 6 as likely pathogenic. Two of the likely pathogenic missense variants were found in the same patient.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: In the man with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, Wang et al. (2026) identified compound heterozygous ADGB missense variants by whole exome sequencing and confirmed them by Sanger sequencing. One of the two variants was c.4859G>A (p.Arg1620Gln, NM_024694.4). Its frequencies were 0.0010 in 1000 Genomes, 0.0001 in ExAC and 0.00285 in gnomAD. SIFT, PolyPhen-2 and CADD (28.2) predicted it to be damaging, and Arg1620 is absolutely conserved across vertebrates.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: The second ADGB variant that Wang et al. (2026) found in the same patient was c.4981A>G (p.Lys1661Glu). It was absent from 1000 Genomes and ExAC and had a frequency of 0.0006 in gnomAD. SIFT, PolyPhen-2 (possibly damaging) and CADD (20.4) predicted it to be deleterious. Lys1661 is conserved in mammals but not in birds, amphibians or fish.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) found by Western blot that ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm. On immunofluorescence, the patient's sperm showed clearly reduced ADGB and reduced PNA (acrosome marker) staining. In control sperm, ADGB was enriched in the acrosome and in the flagellar mitochondrial sheath. AlphaFold3 modeling predicted that the two variants alter the conformation of an alpha-helix and of a C-terminal loop, respectively.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) used STRING analysis and identified the axoneme assembly proteins TTC29 and CFAP47 as candidate ADGB partners. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that both interact with ADGB in sperm. Levels of both proteins were clearly reduced in the patient's sperm. The authors suggested that ADGB may maintain acrosome function and flagellar axoneme assembly by binding TTC29 and CFAP47.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) found that ADGB expression in human testis is low before puberty and peaks in adulthood. In both human and mouse spermatogenic cells, ADGB localized to the acrosome and the flagellum. In mice, Adgb mRNA was highly expressed in adult testis, expressed at low levels in lung and ovary, and peaked in testis at postnatal day 40.

subject: Wang et al. (2026)
object: Wang et al. (2026) reported that the patient's partner conceived with ICSI. 36 oocytes were retrieved and the normal 2PN fertilization rate was 70%. Transfer of a single frozen-thawed blastocyst led to a full-term delivery. The authors noted that all 5 reported couples with ADGB variants had achieved clinical pregnancy with ICSI.
